title: Research papers
summary: These papers study how abelian Galois data detect automorphisms and how the geometry of a boundary controls finite covers over the integers.
overview: This collection develops selected results from two papers on Galois groups and coverings over the integers. The first proves ab-faithfulness for discretely valued fields of mixed characteristic and for positive-dimensional higher local fields. It proves center-freeness of finite-step solvable quotients under ab-faithfulness, and proves slimness directly for infinite finitely generated fields, sub-p-adic fields, and positive-dimensional higher local fields.

The second explains when removing a horizontal divisor leaves solvable covering theory unchanged. Under its arithmetic boundary condition, it also reduces the extension of a representation across the divisor to the same question for its reduction modulo the maximal ideal. The triviality of the étale fundamental group of the integers supplies a basic arithmetic endpoint.
scopeNote: These are selected completed declarations from the ab-faithfulness and solvable-coverings papers. The general Hilbertian application still needs its embedding-problem input, and several examples in the solvable-coverings paper remain outside the selection. Local prototypes are not included.

entries.title: p-ab-faithfulness for discretely valued fields of mixed characteristic
entries.summary: Conjugation on the mod-p abelianized absolute Galois group detects every element of a finite Galois group.
statement: Let $K$ have characteristic $0$ and a discrete valuation with residue characteristic $p>0$. For every finite Galois extension $L/K$,
is injective. In addition, $G_K$ is $p$-ab-faithful. Neither completeness nor Henselianity of the given valuation is assumed in this declaration.
discussion: The field need only carry a discrete valuation of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$; completeness and Henselianity are unnecessary. Detection through a single prime thus applies beyond ordinary local fields. Yamaguchi's Theorem 3.6 proves this using Kummer theory and a reduction to prime-degree extensions, providing an input to the higher-local-field theorem and later applications to solvable Galois quotients.
history: This is Theorem 3.6 of Yamaguchi's 2026 ab-faithfulness paper. Its mixed-characteristic argument uses Kummer theory and a reduction to prime-degree extensions. Within the paper, this valuation-theoretic result supplies an important input for the higher-local-field theorem and subsequent applications to solvable quotients.

entries.title: Ab-faithfulness of absolute Galois groups of positive-dimensional higher local fields
entries.summary: Every positive-dimensional higher local field has an ab-faithful absolute Galois group.
statement: An $n$-dimensional higher local field is defined recursively: dimension $0$ means a finite field, and dimension $n+1$ means a field with a complete discrete valuation whose residue field is $n$-dimensional. The theorem states
$$n>0,\quad K\text{ an }n\text{-dimensional higher local field}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad G_K\text{ is ab-faithful}.$$
discussion: Higher local fields are built through successive complete discrete valuations ending in a finite residue field. The uniform conclusion over finite extensions is useful for studying solvable quotients, where conjugation must remain controlled after passing to open subgroups. Yamaguchi's Theorem 4.2 follows the residue-field towers, combining mixed-characteristic detection with lifting from characteristic-zero residue fields.
history: Theorem 4.2 of Yamaguchi's 2026 paper extends the ab-faithfulness discussion to positive-dimensional higher local fields. The argument follows their residue-field towers, combining mixed-characteristic detection with lifting from characteristic-zero residue fields. The paper then uses these examples in its study of finite-step solvable Galois groups.

entries.title: Trivial centers and slimness of finite-step solvable Galois quotients
entries.summary: Ab-faithfulness forces trivial centers, and the finite-step solvable quotients of finitely generated, sub-p-adic, and higher local fields are slim.
statement: Let $K$ be a field and assume its absolute Galois group $G_K$ is ab-faithful: for every open subgroup $H$ and open normal subgroup $N\subseteq H$, the conjugation action of $H/N$ on the topological abelianization $N^{\mathrm{ab}}$ is faithful. Write $G_K^{(m)}$ for its maximal $m$-step solvable quotient. Then

This statement holds in every characteristic and does not take formal Hilbert 90 or a cyclotomic orientation as extra input. For slimness, the cited second theorem additionally assumes that $K(\mu_{p^\infty})/K$ is infinite for every prime $p\ne\operatorname{char}K$, and that a cyclic extension of degree $p$ exists when $\operatorname{char}K=p>0$. Under these hypotheses, the centralizer of every open subgroup of $G_K^{(m)}$ is trivial.

Slimness is also proved directly, without an ab-faithfulness or orientation hypothesis supplied by the user, for each of these classes of fields: $K$ infinite and finitely generated over its prime field; $K$ admitting an embedding into a finitely generated extension of $\mathbb Q_p$ for a prime $p$; and $K$ a higher local field of positive dimension. In all three cases $G_K^{(m)}$ is slim for every $m\ge2$.
discussion: Finite-step solvable quotients retain only a bounded number of layers of commutators. Center-freeness says that this truncation still leaves no nontrivial element invisible to every inner automorphism, once ab-faithfulness is available.

The argument supplies formal Hilbert 90 from the field’s arithmetic. Corollary 6.6 records a general criterion with explicit cyclotomic and cyclic-extension hypotheses; the field applications then prove the needed inputs for the concrete families in the statement. This turns the criterion into direct slimness theorems for fields used in arithmetic geometry.
history: Corollary 6.6 and the field applications around Example 6.7 of Yamaguchi’s 2026 ab-faithfulness paper connect faithful abelian actions to centers and centralizers in finite-step solvable Galois quotients.

entries.title: The étale fundamental group of Spec Z is trivial
entries.summary: Every geometric base point gives the trivial étale fundamental group of the integers.

The Lean conclusion is that the automorphism group of the geometric fiber functor is a subsingleton.
discussion: In number-field terms, every nontrivial finite extension of $\mathbb Q$ ramifies at some finite prime. This rigidity gives a base case for arguments over the integers: extending a covering across all possible boundary can force it to be trivial. The classical proof uses Minkowski's discriminant theorem; Yamaguchi records it as Example 1.4(1), with SGA 1 providing the language of finite étale covers and fundamental groups.
history: The classical argument uses Minkowski's discriminant theorem to exclude nontrivial number fields unramified at every finite prime. Yamaguchi records the result as Example 1.4(1). SGA 1 supplies the language that expresses the absence of such connected covers as triviality of an étale fundamental group.

entries.title: Removing a divisor preserves the prosolvable fundamental group under the arithmetic boundary condition
entries.summary: Under the arithmetic boundary condition, removing the divisor does not change the maximal prosolvable fundamental group.

discussion: The kernel created in the full fundamental group is topologically perfect, so finite solvable quotients cannot detect it. This explains how the boundary can retain nonabelian information without producing new solvable covers. Yamaguchi's Theorem 2.5 obtains this stronger conclusion by applying the abelian invariance argument after finite étale covers; the perfect-kernel formulation also leads to the subsequent representation-extension result.
history: This is Theorem 2.5 of Yamaguchi's 2026 paper on extending solvable coverings. It advances from abelian invariance to prosolvable invariance by applying the abelian argument after finite étale covers. The formulation through a perfect kernel also prepares the representation-extension result that follows.

entries.title: A representation extends across the boundary exactly when its residual representation does
entries.summary: Under the arithmetic boundary condition, a continuous representation extends across the divisor exactly when its residual representation does.
statement: Let $X$ be connected and locally Noetherian, and let $D$ be a horizontal effective Cartier divisor. Assume $X$ is regular along $D$, each prime component contains a characteristic-$2$ normal-crossings point of $D$, and all reduced boundary components have geometrically integral generic fibers over $\mathbb Q$ after every connected finite étale cover of $X$. Put $U=X\setminus D$. Let $A$ be a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field $k_A$ of characteristic $p$, carrying its maximal-ideal-adic topology. Here $\bar\rho$ is reduction modulo the maximal ideal, with the discrete topology on $k_A$. When the factorization of $\rho$ exists, it is unique.
discussion: The extension problem over a complete Noetherian local ring with finite residue field becomes a question over finite coefficients. A perfect boundary kernel contributes no obstruction through the successive abelian pieces of the congruence filtration, so the residual test suffices at every adic level. Corollary 2.6 of Yamaguchi's 2026 paper applies the preceding perfect-kernel theorem in exactly this way.
history: Corollary 2.6 of Yamaguchi's 2026 solvable-coverings paper follows the perfect-kernel theorem. It applies that geometric result to continuous linear representations, using the congruence filtration of a complete local coefficient ring. The conclusion connects extension of arithmetic coverings with reduction modulo the maximal ideal.
